findings.summary: AddressSanitizer (ASan) is a code sanitizer that detects memory bugs via compiler-inserted runtime instrumentation. It uses a shadow memory scheme to find heap-use-after-free, heap-buffer-overflow, stack-buffer-overflow, and global-buffer-overflow. ASan trades about 73% processing time and 240% memory for its coverage. It does not detect uninitialized reads (handled by MSan) or all arbitrary corruption, and adjacent struct/class buffers may overflow due to backward compatibility design choices.

mechanisms.title: Shadow memory scheme
mechanisms.explanation: ASan maps application memory to a shadow memory region where each 8-byte chunk is represented by one shadow byte. Poison values in shadow bytes mark freed, overflowed, or out-of-bounds regions; runtime checks inspect these bytes to detect invalid accesses.

mechanisms.title: Runtime instrumentation and redzones
mechanisms.explanation: The compiler inserts checks at runtime to validate memory accesses against shadow metadata. Redzone markers (fa/fb) surround allocated and freed regions to catch out-of-bounds and use-after-free errors respectively.
